newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Ciampi sees Italy in first group of EMU members.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi sees Italy in first group of EMU members.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Wednesday Italy would do its utmost to be in the first group of nations to join Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999.
"Italy will do everything it can to be among the first countries that will take part in the first phase of EMU," Ciampi told journalists after a meeting with his Austrian counterpart Viktor Klima.
Ciampi said he was convinced that Italy would reduce its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product in 1997, a key condition for membership in EMU.
"Our budget polices have made it possible to reduce the deficit to three percent. It's an ambitious goal but we are convinced we will reach it," he said.

The Italian government's budget proposal aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire from next year's deficit to help squeeze the country into EMU. European Union member countries will have to qualify for EMU membership in March of 1997.
Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said he and Ciampi had agreed there should be no watering down of the so-called Maastricht criteria for EMU.
Apart from a three percent deficit requirement, the criteria include strict public debt, inflation, interest rate and exchange rate thresholds for membership.
"Italy and Austria agree that there must not be a change in the convergence criteria, which ensure stability," Klima said.
Klima said he attached great importance to Italian membership in the single currency, since Italy was Austria's second most important trading partner.
"It is of special importance to Austria that Italy will become a member of EMU as soon as possible," he said.

Klima applauded Italy for its attempts to be among the first wave of EMU members, saying the markets had reacted positively to the lira's return to the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) last week.
"The markets have recognised the efforts of the Italian government. The exchange rate has developed even better than its original level," he said.

The lira last traded at around 980 lira to the German mark, Europe's anchor currency, above its central parity of 990 lira. Italy was readmitted to the ERM after it originally left the system, seen as a precursor to monetary union, following a wave of currency turmoil and a steep devaluation in 1992.

Klima reiterated that he was confident Austria itself would meet all the Maastricht criteria for European economic and monetary union "in a sustainable way". -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
